items.intro: Our picks of under-the-radar gems from this month’s new releases. This edition includes chilly thrillers of domestic deception, a period horror comedy and a concert film that unites two generational talents.

items.intro: From recent discoveries yet to begin their distribution journey, to hidden gems that slipped through the cracks—these standout films have been out of reach for most of our members, until now.

items.title: With Friends Like These: twenty wildly entertaining buddy comedies
items.intro: With Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine galloping into theaters, Rory Doherty writes in praise of twenty essential buddy comedies—from The Sting to Superbad—to watch with your friends or your frenemies.

items.title: Neon Screams: twenty films where horror and noir bleed into one
items.intro: Both horror and noir use heavy, stylized atmospheres to communicate otherworldly dread and terror. Travis Woods counts off 20 essential films that combine both genres to chilling effect.

items.title: Fallen Angels and Human Flies: on screens and shelves this month
items.intro: The collected works of a Japanese New Wave master, David Bowie’s most luminous star vehicle and Bong Joon Ho’s monster movie are among the selections in this month’s edition of Shelf Life.

items.title: Scarred for Life: our crew shares the unexpectedly formative movies we watched way too young
items.intro: From The Sixth Sense to When a Stranger Calls, the Letterboxd crew shares the unexpectedly traumatizing films we watched through our fingers as children.

items.title: Re-Enter the Void: 20 paranoid sci-fi mind-benders from the early 2000s
items.intro: With this year’s sci-fi movies harking back to the surrealist paranoia of the early 2000s, Payton McCarty-Simas curates twenty of the trippiest titles from the aughts to take a trip down memory lane.
